## How to review

2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.

10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.

## 1. The signs sent upon the people of Fir'awn  (`#the-signs-sent-upon-the-people-of-firawn`)

Cited ayat: 7:130-135, 17:101, 27:12

> **7:130** وَلَقَدْ أَخَذْنَآ ءَالَ فِرْعَوْنَ بِٱلسِّنِينَ وَنَقْصٍ مِّنَ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (7:130): God seized the people of Fir'awn with years of drought and a shortage of fruits, so that they might remember.

**c2** (7:131): When good came to them they said it was theirs, and if evil struck them they took Musa and those with him as an omen; God says that their omen is with Him, but most of them do not know.

**c3** (7:132): They said that whatever sign he brought to bewitch them, they would not believe him.

**c4** (7:133): God sent upon them the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood as signs in detail; they were arrogant and a criminal people.

**c5** (7:134): When the plague fell upon them they said to Musa that he should call upon his Lord by the covenant He had made with him; if he removed the plague they would believe him and send the Children of Israel with him.

**c6** (7:135): When God removed the plague from them for a term which they were to reach, they broke their word.

**c7** (17:101): God says that He gave Musa nine clear signs, and that Fir'awn said to him that he thought him bewitched.

**c8** (27:12): Musa was told to put his hand into his bosom and it would come out white without harm, among nine signs to Fir'awn and his people, who were a defiantly disobedient people.

### One-minute summary

God seized the people of Fir'awn with years of drought and a shortage of fruits, and then sent the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood as signs [c1][c4]. When the plague fell on them they asked Musa to call upon his Lord, but broke their word once it was removed [c5][c6].

### Complete story

God seized the people of Fir'awn with years of drought and a shortage of fruits, so that they might remember [c1]. When good came to them they said it was theirs, and if evil struck them they took Musa and those with him as an omen; God says their omen is with Him [c2]. They said that whatever sign he brought, they would not believe him [c3].

God sent upon them the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood as signs in detail; they were arrogant and a criminal people [c4]. When the plague fell upon them they said to Musa that he should call upon his Lord, and that if he removed it they would believe and send the Children of Israel with him [c5]. When God removed it for a term which they were to reach, they broke their word [c6].

God says that He gave Musa nine clear signs [c7], and that among nine signs Musa was told to put his hand into his bosom and it would come out white without harm [c8].

### Deep study

The chapter has the first seizing [c1][c2][c3], the signs in detail [c4], the people's promise and the breaking of it [c5][c6], and verses that name nine signs [c7][c8]. The Quran lists signs by name here [c4] and speaks of nine elsewhere [c7][c8]; it does not say that the listed signs are among the nine or that they are the nine. The omen is placed with God and not with Musa [c2].

### Kids mode

God sent hard times and signs on the people of Fir'awn so that they might remember [c1][c4]. They asked Musa to pray to his Lord, but when the trouble went away they broke their word [c5][c6].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the people credited good to themselves and blamed Musa for harm [c2]. Another is that a promise made in trouble was broken when the trouble was lifted [c5][c6].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: the order, length and number of the plagues beyond those named in 7:133, or how many years of drought are meant.
- The Arabic words for the flood (tufan) and the lice (qummal) are understood in more than one way; a scholar should decide the renderings.
- Not established: what the nine signs are; the signs named here are not assumed to be among them.
- Not established: how long the term was after which the people broke their word.
- The verses do not say how Musa's prayer was made or in what words.
